chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Penguin sessions after the war and a new Queens Terrace band
summary: Penguin recordings with an entirely new band back at the Queens Terrace in 1945.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: He made, John Henry, when I got back in '45--I don't mean '45, I'm sorry, in '52 I meant.
No, he died three years ago.
So he stayed your manager most of those years?
(Side A of Tape 4 ended at this point.)
(Side B of Tape 4 begins at this point.)
Penguin Records were made when you came back from overseas the first time, in 1935?
Actually you had been back for a while, you had Kenny Rickman on trumpet; he didn't work for you that long, did he?
No, he didn't stay with me too long
We went back to the Queens Terrace for a while. I had an entirely new band.
I don't know who your regular piano player was.
George Fauntleroy on saxophone and Kenny Rickman.
This is 1945; the first records for Penguin.
Would you want a copy of this made?
